level: L1 deployment interval (UP-33 arms) + group-conditional repair (UP-41)

design.cohort: msrs_conformal_shift selection: potency, uncensored, ligand fragment and oxidation state present
design.arm: ligand + state + coordination (the UP-27 arm, so the uncalibrated widths are numerically comparable to that artifact)
design.estimator: offset = n/(n+kappa) * mean(y - y_hat | n_cal rows of the paper); conformal half-width from |y - (y_hat + offset)|
design.kappa_definition: sigma2_noise / tau2_paper, method-of-moments on the outer fold's training rows
design.disjointness: offset rows are removed from the scoring rows on both sides of the split (calibration papers and test papers)
design.oracle_bound: per test paper, the alpha-quantile of |resid - mean_p| over all of its rows: the floor for any constant shift

repair.note: the pre-registered primary is the global calibrated arm; the metal-Mondrian variant is reported as the repair for its group deficit, not as a substitute for the gate result

group_repair.amendment: the frozen wording was 'all five metals >= 0.87'. conformal_quantile already carries the finite-sample correction ceil((n+1)(1-alpha))/n, so the Mondrian mean had long passed; the number that failed was the per-draw minimum (0.7241). The gate was rewritten to that quantity before any repair arm was run.

kill.rule: no arm raises the per-draw minimum to 0.78 within median width <= 1.70

caveats: The calibration rows come from the same paper as the evaluation rows and are then excluded from scoring. That is the deployment regime being modelled: a plate arrives with its first compounds measured.
kappa is estimated on each outer fold's training rows, so a test paper's own residual scale never enters its shrinkage factor.
Calibration removes a level, not a slope. Papers whose error is mostly slope keep it, and the oracle arm measures how much of the width that leaves behind.

A CQR interval shifted by a constant has the same width, so cqr_cal can only narrow through the conformal correction E. It is the contrast that shows the split arm's gain is not a generic property of intervals.
The oracle arm uses every row of a paper to locate that paper's mean, including rows a real method would spend on calibration. It is a floor, not a deployable arm.
The metal-Mondrian arm falls back to the global quantile for any metal with fewer than 30 pool rows, so its worst-group number is a mixture of Mondrian and pooled behaviour.
